summary: Call-site review (not floorplan/line-count): Zoomies has real deep modules—especially PNGMetadata, and to a large extent ScreenRecordingService and SettingsStore—plus a leaky shared encoding helper around screenshots. Tiny helpers like UniqueFileURLLogic are useful, not costly abstractions.
findings: PNGMetadata is the clearest deep module: callers only call embed/extract/extractEditorState/isPNG; chunk parsing, iTXt assembly, CRC, and Zoomies-chunk stripping stay inside Sources/PNGMetadata.swift. Production callers: WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic (embed) and WorkflowReopenMetadataLogic (extract). Callers still choose *policy* (when to embed prompt+original vs editorState-only; 50MB skip in WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic)—that is layering, not a leak of PNG format.

ScreenRecordingService and SettingsStore hide useful complexity behind narrow interfaces. AppDelegate/Tray drive recording with start/stop/state/elapsed/callbacks and never touch SCStream/session/finalize. Settings callers use load/settings/update/didRepair; path migration, JSON, normalization, and atomic writes stay private. UniqueFileURLLogic is the contrast case: a small useful helper (unique _2/_3 names), reused by recording/screenshot/clipboard/scratchpad—not a costly abstraction.

ScreenshotService’s hotkey surface is relatively deep (captureArea/captureFullScreen hide ScreenCaptureKit, save, sound, workflow kickoff), but ScreenshotServiceCoreLogic is a leaky shared kitchen: EditorCanvasView, ScreenshotWorkflowController, WorkflowReopenMetadataLogic, and WorkflowImagePersistenceLogic must call pngData/bitmapRepresentation themselves. beginPostCaptureFlow’s fat overload also forces coordination of initialImage / persistence Task / counter. Large ScreenRecordingService internals alone would not prove depth; depth here is evidenced by the simple caller surface.
decisions: Judged depth from verified call sites and what callers must know, not file size or work/code-views floorplan grouping.
Treated UniqueFileURLLogic/DirectoryPurgeLogic-style enums as small useful helpers; treated ScreenshotServiceCoreLogic as a leaky shared encoding surface rather than a deep module boundary.
Did not assign numeric depth scores; assessment is qualitative with file:line evidence only.

open_issues: AppDelegate busy-state orchestration across screenshot/recording/scratchpad/video-rename is cross-feature coordination, not a leak of ScreenRecordingService internals—worth not conflating with module depth.
SettingsStore does not hide the Settings schema; UI and services still know field names—depth is about persistence/migration, not domain model encapsulation.
Hypothesis only: further extraction of a single ‘image encode + metadata’ facade might deepen the screenshot boundary; not verified as net win.
next_steps: If orchestrating follow-up design: preserve PNGMetadata’s simple embed/extract surface; avoid treating CoreLogic reuse as proof of a clean ScreenshotService boundary.
No code changes required from this review; existing user work left untouched.
